findings.title: Only one weekday bar has a value

location.description: The Orders by weekday chart in the right-hand card.

findings.viewer_experience: The viewer can read only the Saturday figure and has to estimate the other six days from bar heights, because the chart has no value scale.

current.value: A single number, 126, sits above the highlighted Saturday bar; the other six bars carry no number and the chart has no value axis.

findings.target: A viewer can read the approximate value of any weekday, not only Saturday.
findings.fix_direction: Give the viewer a way to read the other bars, with a scale or a small number on each.
findings.source: Tufte, The Visual Display of Quantitative Information, on data-ink and labelling

closed_when.check: Look at the weekday chart and check that a value for a weekday other than Saturday can be read.

findings.title: The comparison with last month is small and grey

location.description: The line of small grey text under each of the four headline figures.

findings.viewer_experience: The viewer sees the headline number clearly but is likely to skip the comparison under it, though it says whether the number is good news.

current.value: The comparison with October is set in small grey text under each figure.

findings.target: The comparison is readable at the same glance as the headline figure.
findings.fix_direction: Give the comparison more weight so it is read together with the figure.

closed_when.check: Look at the four headline figures and check that the comparison under each is easy to read.
